environment.description: Same Actix-web binary deployed behind an envoy sidecar proxy (v1.28) with a custom Lua filter that injects a Content-Security-Policy response header on all text/html responses. The CSP directive is: script-src 'self' https://cdn.example.com/lib/search-highlight.min.js'sha384-oqVuAfXRKap7fdgcCY5uykM6+R9GqQ8K/uxy9rx7HNQlGYl1kPzQho1wx4JwY8wC' https://cdn.example.com/lib/dom-purify.min.js'sha384-Li9vy3DqF8tnTXuiaAJuML3ky+er10rcgNR/VqsVpcw+ThHmYcwiB1pbOxEb2V2I'; style-src 'self'; default-src 'self'; object-src 'none'. The SRI integrity attributes are enforced by the CSP require-sri-for directive (deprecated but supported in the deployed Chrome-based internal browser fleet v89-v94). Additionally, the envoy filter strips any inline script that doesn't match a nonce (no nonce is provided, so ALL inline scripts are blocked including the legitimate one in the footer). The net effect is that injected script tags and inline event handlers cannot execute because the CSP blocks inline script execution (no 'unsafe-inline' in script-src).

config.infrastructure: AWS NLB -> Envoy 1.28 sidecar -> EC2 (Amazon Linux 2)
config.envoy_lua_filter: injects CSP header on text/html responses
config.require_sri_for: script style (enforced via CSP on internal browser fleet)
config.browser_fleet: Internal Chromium v89-v94 with require-sri-for support
